name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: North Dakota's at-large district leans Republican by about 18 points
Incumbent Julie Fedorchak won renomination and holds a large fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Fedorchak near 96% to win
Challenger Trygve Hammer has raised only a small fraction of the incumbent's total
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Republican: an R+18 district, a renominated incumbent with over $1 million on hand against a challenger with under $70,000, and markets pricing a Democratic win at just 3%. With no competitive polling or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, this stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or a dramatic statewide political shift could narrow the race, but nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Julie Fedorchak seeks a second term representing North Dakota's at-large House seat, a district that favored Republicans by roughly 18 points in recent cycles. She enters the general election as a heavy favorite, having comfortably secured her party's nomination and built a commanding financial position with about $1.1 million on hand.

Democratic nominee Trygve Hammer faces steep odds. He has raised under $200,000 and holds less than $70,000 in cash, with no outside spending on either side reported so far. Two independent candidates also appear on the ballot but show no measurable campaign activity. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance, and no public polling of the race has emerged. Absent unexpected developments, Fedorchak is positioned to win decisively.
